core_obligations: Reduce to injective preservation: by hypothesis (e) of the comparison lemma the two global section functors agree, so it is enough to show that g^{-1} sends injective abelian sheaves on D to injective abelian sheaves on C (proof lines 670-673).

Verify the adjoint-pair criterion: use the standard criterion for an adjoint pair to preserve injectives, whose hypothesis is exactness of the left adjoint; the left adjoint of g^{-1} is g_! = f^{-1} in the notation of the comparison lemma, which is exact (proof lines 673-678).

Conclude the isomorphisms: with injectives preserved and degree-zero sections equal, the derived functors agree, giving RGamma(C, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(D, F), and the local form RGamma(U, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(u(U), F) follows by applying the same argument to the induced sites over U and u(U); all identifications are functorial in F (statement lines 653-666, proof lines 669-678).
proof_roadmap: Use the hypothesis that global sections agree to reduce the comparison of derived functors to preservation of injectives by g^{-1} (proof lines 670-673).
Apply the adjoint-pair criterion for preservation of injectives, checking exactness of the left adjoint g_! = f^{-1} (proof lines 673-678).
Read off the global and local isomorphisms asserted in the statement (proof lines 669-678 with statement lines 653-666).
difficulty_reason: The lemma transfers cohomology from a site D to a site C along a comparison functor u satisfying the hypotheses of the standard comparison lemma, giving RGamma(C, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(D, F), its local form RGamma(U, g^{-1}F) = RGamma(u(U), F) and the resulting H^p identifications, functorially in F (statement lines 653-666). The proof is short but its one substantive point is that the reduction to preservation of injectives is legitimate: degree zero is the hypothesis of the comparison lemma, and the injective preservation comes from the adjoint-pair criterion whose input is exactness of the left adjoint g_! = f^{-1}, which has to be identified correctly (proof lines 670-678). The claim is H2: two cited inputs assembled in the right order, with the local statement following formally.
